one_liner: Sparse-matrix code generator and kernel library; SC17 Cholesky 3.8x average over Eigen, 1.5x over CHOLMOD on fixed patterns.
what_it_does: Sympiler specializes sparse triangular solve and Cholesky factorization for one fixed sparsity pattern. It inspects the pattern ahead of time and emits specialized C code for the numeric phase. The repository now has two parts: the legacy code generator (code_gen/, marked 'under major changes', built against MKL and SuiteSparse through MKLROOT/SUITEROOT) and a static library, sym_sparse_blas, of C-style kernels taking raw CSC/CSR pointers (sptrsv_csc, sptrsv_csr_levelset, sptrsv_csr_lbc, spic0, spilu0, spldl, spcholesky, spmv). Neither part is a drop-in for Eigen or CHOLMOD.
how_it_is_fast: Symbolic analysis (dependency-graph reach for triangular solve, elimination tree for Cholesky) runs once, before the numeric phase. Variable Iteration Space Pruning (VI-Prune) then shrinks the loops to the structurally nonzero work, and 2D Variable-Sized Blocking (VS-Block) groups columns into supernodes so dense BLAS kernels apply. Because loop bounds are known at generation time, it can also unroll, peel, vectorize and tile. The library kernels add level-set and load-balanced level coarsening (LBC) OpenMP schedules for parallel triangular solve.
when_to_use: Repeated triangular solves or Cholesky refactorizations with the same sparsity pattern and changing values (Newton steps, time stepping, preconditioner re-application)
Single-core SPD factorization of SuiteSparse-sized matrices (13.7K-1M rows, 0.7-5M nonzeros in the paper) where CHOLMOD is the bottleneck
Research or prototyping of inspector-executor sparse kernels; the code is MIT-licensed and readable
When raw CSC/CSR pointer kernels without a matrix class are acceptable
when_not_to_use: Patterns that change every solve: per the paper, inspection plus code generation costs 6-197x a triangular solve and only pays off over many reuses
LU, QR or unsymmetric direct solves: the paper covers only triangular solve and Cholesky (the library adds IC0, ILU0 and LDL kernels, with no published comparison)

Production code that needs a maintained, documented API: last commit 2023-07, the code generator README says it is 'under major changes', and the docs site (sympiler.com) now serves a placeholder demo page
Multicore or distributed Cholesky: the SC17 results are single-core
Non-x86 Linux builds: CMake hard-codes -march=x86-64 -mavx2 on Linux

integration.form: static lib (sym_sparse_blas) plus a separate code generator
integration.dependencies: BLAS (OpenBLAS default, MKL or Apple Accelerate), METIS, aggregation git submodule; optional OpenMP, TBB, SCOTCH, PAPI; the legacy code_gen needs MKL and SuiteSparse
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 (AVX2 forced by CMake), macOS; CI on Ubuntu and macOS

gotchas: The README badge says Apache (copied from micromatch); LICENSE.txt is MIT
Clone with --recursive, because the aggregation submodule is required
CMake adds -w, which suppresses all compiler warnings
Paper benchmarks used GCC 5.4 and OpenBLAS 0.2.19 on a 2014 Haswell-E CPU; there are no recent numbers
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose Sympiler over BaSpaCho when you are on a CPU, the pattern is fixed, and you want generated or simple single-core supernodal code with an MIT license. Choose it over Ginkgo or AMGCL when you need an exact direct triangular solve or Cholesky rather than an iterative method, and BaSpaCho is the more maintained choice for GPU or multithreaded Cholesky.
verified_claims_summary: The SC17 paper measures generated code against Eigen and CHOLMOD on 11 SuiteSparse SPD matrices, single core, i7-5820K at 3.3GHz with turbo off, GCC 5.4 -O3 with OpenBLAS 0.2.19, median of 5 runs. Triangular solve averages 1.49x over Eigen. Cholesky averages 3.8x over Eigen (up to 6.3x) and 1.5x over CHOLMOD (up to 2.4x), with symbolic and compile cost excluded.
status_note: Stale since July 2023 (44 stars, 135 commits) but MIT-licensed. The kernel library is small enough to vendor; the code generator is half-maintained research code.
